resources.string: opensensor.space connects to compatible sensor devices over Bluetooth Low Energy and copies their Parquet files onto this phone. It asks for Bluetooth scanning and connecting. It never asks for location. Network access is used only to reach a sensor device on your own Wi-Fi network, found with mDNS. There is no cloud endpoint, and nothing leaves this phone unless you share it.
Bluetooth permission was denied. Enable it in system settings to find your sensors.

Bring the phone near a compatible Bluetooth sensor device. Current firmware advertises as AQ-xxxx.
On first connection, enter the device’s 6-digit pairing code. Read it from its display, or obtain the owner PIN over USB for a device without a display.
Turn on your sensor and keep this phone close. It shows up here in a few seconds.
Your known sensors are listed below. Move closer to one to connect, or look at its saved history anytime.
This removes the saved device, its Wi-Fi access and automatic collection from this phone. Files already collected stay here. The device may still appear under Nearby while it is advertising.

Collects from known devices over Wi-Fi when this phone holds their token, otherwise over their Bluetooth pairing. Up to two transfers run at once with a progress notification, so you can leave the app. Devices with an open connection are skipped.

Set time gives a date to readings from now on. Finalize writes the readings waiting in memory to a short file so they can be synced now.

Sends this phone’s clock (%1$s) to the sensor. Only readings taken after this moment get a date and a dated folder. Readings already recorded stay undated and are never rewritten. Do this only if you trust the phone’s time.

The sensor keeps the newest rows in memory until its file interval ends. Finalizing writes them to the card now as a short Parquet file so you can sync everything up to this moment. On firmware v6 it also closes the open file’s row groups already on the card. It does not change the interval.

One system dialog. Android then watches for this device by itself, wakes the app when it is in range and lets it use the network in the background while the device is present.
The Bluetooth link is dropped for the dialog, since the device must be advertising, and restored afterwards.

Runs as a background job with a progress notification. A summary appears only when new files arrived. Android picks the exact moment within each period and needs a battery that is not low. Joining a Wi-Fi network also starts a check. Files are pulled and verified exactly as with Sync all, and the device is never asked to delete anything.

The device makes a new token and drops every Wi-Fi session. Every phone, including this one, must fetch the new token over Bluetooth before syncing over Wi-Fi again. Do this if a phone that had the token was lost.
